annotations.shape: hand-written bytes (tools/write_raw_fixtures.py holds them as typed literals): a header block containing a line that is neither name: value nor a fold (the region must fail open past it, D2), and a multipart/mixed (boundary b1-malformed) whose close delimiter is missing entirely
annotations.provenance: the bytes are frozen in fixtures/raw/SHA256SUMS and checked by tests/test_fixtures.py; a generator would be encoding the assumption under test (D11's raw hand-written set); the measured spike (a03, b01) covers both defects and their stdlib behaviour
annotations.phase_numbering: the design document's phases: 0 = the Phase 0 skeleton walker (spans, decode chain, accounted regions, gaps), 1 = the Phase 1 parser (header projection, body views, attachment manifest), 2 = routing and statuses, 3 = threading and time evidence
annotations.labels_are_typed: every value was read out of the fixture bytes with a hex-editor-style line dump and typed by a model from the design rules (D2/D3/D9), never copied out of the walker; labels_provenance is spec because a model wrote them, not a person
annotations.span_conventions: the malformed line is its own paragraph: name empty, name_span of length zero, value_span the line's content, parse_status unknown -- and the header region does not end there (D2 fail-open), so X-After and the fields after it are still fields; the child body spans end before the delimiter's leading CRLF (these hand-written bytes carry no spare empty line)
annotations.expected_gaps: headers.malformed_line on part 1 (the non-header line) and body.boundary_disagreement on part 1 (the declared boundary is not closed: the bytes disagree with the declared grammar and nothing is guessed)
annotations.not_yet_labelled: the status the Phase 2 parser will give this message (the closed nine-member vocabulary), views (phase 1), thread edges and TimeEvents (phase 3)

value: the design records the gap when the declared grammar and the bytes disagree (D3, the registry's boundary_disagreement) but does not say whether a missing close delimiter is that gap or the sibling no_boundary_found: this label reads missing-close as boundary_disagreement (the boundary IS found, its close is not) and asks the design to confirm the split, because the two ids lead a reader to different conclusions about what the message contains
